name: rg1_regression_safe
stressor: regression-safe change (fix X, keep Y): a small CSV-like record codec ships TWO features that share one quoting convention -- ENCODING (feature Y: correct, with passing tests) and DECODING (feature X: buggy). The decoder's quoted-field scanner does not handle the doubled-quote escape, so any field with an embedded quote is truncated/mis-split and round-trip breaks. The task is to fix DECODING without regressing ENCODING. The trap: a broad fix that changes the shared escape convention, rewrites the quoting rules, or 'simplifies' the encoder to agree with a still-wrong decoder will silently break feature Y.
source_note: Purpose-built DSV record codec authored for this benchmark: dsv.py (encode_record/decode_record sharing the doubled-quote escape convention), table.py (dumps/loads built on dsv), and a unittest suite test_dsv.py whose encode tests pin feature Y and all pass. setup() corrupts exactly one unique block inside dsv.decode_record -- the doubled-quote peek-ahead -- so the FIRST quote of an escaped "" pair is taken as the closing quote and the field is truncated; plain fields and delimiter-quoted fields decode fine, so the symptom only appears for values containing an embedded quote. reference_fix reverts that one block in the DECODER ONLY, leaving the encoder untouched. The oracle re-runs the WHOLE suite in a fresh `python -B -m unittest` subprocess (must be all green, encode tests intact) AND, in a second fresh child, exercises BOTH directions on inputs the agent never saw: unseen decode lines must parse correctly (X fixed), the encoder must still emit the exact canonical quoted/escaped form recomputed independently in the oracle (Y guard), and decode(encode(x))==x plus table.loads(table.dumps(rows))==rows must hold (the conjunction).
discriminator: The agent must satisfy a CONJUNCTION that spans two coupled features: feature X (decode escaped quotes correctly, on unseen inputs) AND feature Y (encode still emits the canonical escaped form, asserted independently by the oracle) AND their round-trip. Because both directions live in the same module and share one escape convention, the cheap fix is tempting: rewrite the codec, change the escape character, or make the encoder match a half-fixed decoder. A bounded-slice agent re-reads dsv.py each turn and keeps the encoder + its passing tests live in the working set, so it localizes the missing doubled-quote peek-ahead in decode_record and edits only that block, preserving Y. A growing-transcript agent that read the encoder early, then iterated on the decoder under bloat tends to lose the encoder's constraint from attention and 'fix' decoding with a broad edit that regresses encoding (or weakens an encode test), failing the Y guard or the round-trip on inputs it never saw -- the harness-quality axis is holding the keep-Y invariant live while changing X, which truncation/transcript-bloat erodes.
